move: endless strip holds then expo-slides one frame, centre scaled up
how: A track of six frames (three photos, three gradients) is tripled so the strip is endless; each frame is 640px wide with a 40px gap. The whole loop is divided into six slots; within a slot the strip holds for 55% then slides one frame left over the remaining 45% with expo.inOut, computed each frame as a fractional index and applied as translate3d on the track. Frames scale from 1 at centre down to 0.88 and dim to 0.5 opacity one frame away, and each frame's image counter-translates 30px per frame of distance for parallax. A dot row highlights the current index (scale 1.5, white). Because six slots move six frames and the strip repeats every six, the last frame matches the first exactly.
adapt: Replace the items array (class, title, number), frame width and gap, and the hold fraction (0.55). Keep the expo.inOut slide, the 0.12 scale falloff and N slots == N frames so the loop closes.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the tripled track and dots inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one proxy tween ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none) whose onUpdate runs the per-frame placement (track translate, frame scale/opacity, dot state), replacing the fx.register seek loop; the centre offset must be derived from el width.
caveats: no GSAP timeline in the source; motion is an fx.register seek function writing inline transforms (gsap.parseEase only)
